decisions.quote: In our replications, the effect of God salience on AI reliance is not statistically different from zero (Studies 1, 2a, 2b, 3, and 5 produced effect sizes, measured by  r , of 0.03, 0.02, 0.03, 0.002, and 0.01, respectively—in contrast to the original effect sizes reported for each of the respective studies of 0.19, 0.15, 0.14, 0.11, and 0.19).  Fig. 1  omits a conceptual replication of Study 1 that produced a nonsignificant effect in the  opposite  direction of the original Study 1,  t (279) = −1.78,  P  = 0.077,  r  = −0.10 and a replication of Study 5 that successfully replicated the original result but whose experimental materials included a typographical error that presented inconsistent and potentially confusing information to participants in one experimental condition,  t (872) = 2.26,  P  = 0.024,  r  = 0.09. Although the majority of our replications produced results directionally consistent with those of Karataş and Cutright, our results imply that if the effect exists, it is so small that the original studies lacked the power to detect it.
decisions.reason: The authors exclude the extra Study 5 run from their primary analysis because a typographical error presented inconsistent and confusing information to participants, and their clean direct replication of Study 5 along with all other replications (Studies 1, 2a, 2b, and 3) found effects not statistically different from zero. Following the authors' overall judgment that the published effects did not replicate, the outcome is failed rather than mixed.
